Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
You're welcome. Now, who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone speak to him before it went into the gradebook?
This meeting is over. I'm leaving.
You asked for this meeting, Hale. Sit down and answer my question, or I walk straight to the principal's office and we have it there instead. Who decided?

Then I'm going upstairs to the principal now, and I'll be asking why your own procedure says a parent gets a call before any mark is entered. I'm writing down that you refused to explain the zero. You'll have my email tonight.
Because my son has a zero and you haven't told me why. Withdraw it, or give me one reason it's there.
